sources.name: OGC API - Common - Part 1: Core 1.0
sources.role: landing page, API definition and conformance declaration contract
verified_facts: The landing page exposes links to the API definition and conformance declaration resources.
The server supports GET on {root}/conformance and the successful response lists implemented OGC API conformance-class URIs in conformsTo.
Encoding classes such as HTML and JSON are separately declared capabilities rather than implicit guarantees.
semantic_limits: A conformance declaration states implemented modules; it does not validate the accuracy, freshness or completeness of a particular terrain response.
An API definition or HTTP 200 response is not exact HMLR geometry, ODN height or parcel measurement evidence.
Content negotiation and representation format must not create a business row.

sources.name: OGC API - Features - Part 2: Coordinate Reference Systems by Reference 1.0.1
sources.role: supported CRS, storage CRS and coordinate epoch contract
verified_facts: A collection advertises supported CRS identifiers in its crs property, whose default is OGC CRS84.
If all features are stored in one CRS, storageCrs identifies that CRS and its value must occur in the collection's supported CRS list.
For a dynamic storage CRS, storageCrsCoordinateEpoch should provide the coordinate epoch of the stored coordinates.
semantic_limits: storageCrs and response CRS describe feature-coordinate handling; they do not identify an orthometric vertical datum or certify elevation units.
Reprojection into a supported CRS does not improve source positional or height accuracy.
A collection-level coordinate epoch cannot be silently treated as a per-feature observation date.

sources.name: OGC API - Features - Part 3: Filtering 1.0
sources.role: queryables, filter language, filter CRS and subset contract
verified_facts: Each filterable collection exposes a Queryables resource represented as JSON Schema.
filter, filter-lang and filter-crs parameters describe enhanced selection criteria; invalid values produce a 400 response.
When filter is combined with bbox, datetime or property filters, all predicates are logically connected with AND.
semantic_limits: The Queryables schema is a virtual resource view for filtering and is not necessarily the schema of retrievable feature objects.
A successful filter returns a subset; it does not prove the complete source collection was read.
A feature passing a filter does not prove exact parcel containment, elevation semantics or source accuracy.

sources.name: Common Query Language (CQL2) 1.0
sources.role: boolean scalar, spatial and temporal predicate contract
verified_facts: A CQL2 filter is a logically connected expression of one or more scalar, spatial or temporal predicates.
Standardized spatial comparison functions are evaluated using Simple Features semantics and return Boolean results.
CQL2 defines text and JSON encodings that can be carried by filtering APIs.
semantic_limits: A TRUE predicate is only a selection result and must not be interpreted as a terrain measurement.
Spatial predicate evaluation remains invalid for parcel QA unless geometry identity, CRS and axis semantics are bound.
Supported functions or successful expression parsing do not validate the authority or accuracy of the underlying source.
